title: Reuse wording when meaning and context match
text: Use the same authoritative terms and consistent sentence patterns for equivalent instructions or descriptions when their meaning and context match. Reuse reviewed wording or an applicable reviewed template rather than introduce synonyms for variety. Before reuse, compare the actors, actions, conditions, quantities, scope, timing, and effects. Retain every real difference; do not make distinct operations appear equivalent merely to produce matching sentences. In descriptive text, keep the explanation coherent as a whole, with clear references and logical progression, instead of repeating a procedural pattern mechanically. Preserve externally controlled strings and machine-significant literals exactly.
exceptions: A template is reusable only within its reviewed applicability. Do not copy an instruction into a different role, product version, failure branch, or risk context without checking its requirements and dependencies.

Consistency does not require identical wording for different effects or repetitive wording where a clear reference preserves descriptive coherence. Do not omit required safety or security context for stylistic uniformity.

When authoritative external labels differ, retain each exact label and explain its mapping to the intended concept. Do not silently rename the external element. Escalate ambiguous equivalence or conflicting requirements to the responsible editor or technical owner.
Examples judge local consistency, not global lexical approval. Supporting target IDs refer to planned work, not canonical relation endpoints or delegated source allocations.

segments.text: Example glossary: deployment log is the authoritative term for each deployment's diagnostic record. Equivalent instructions: Open the deployment log for the test deployment. Open the deployment log for the staging deployment.

allowed.rationale: The same operation and concept use the same wording; only the deployment scope changes. The example glossary is local, not an IT-STE vocabulary approval.

segments.text: The import service checks the file format automatically. If that check fails, the operator reviews the error report.

allowed.rationale: Different actors and actions remain distinct, and the description progresses through an explicit failure condition instead of forcing both sentences into a reader-action template.

segments.text: Example glossary: deployment log is the authoritative term for each deployment's diagnostic record. Equivalent instructions: Open the deployment log for the test deployment. Inspect the rollout journal for the staging deployment. The wording changes only for variety.

not_allowed.rationale: The stylistic substitutions suggest a different record or action without a technical distinction. Reuse the reviewed term and pattern as in the positive example.

segments.text: Editorial context: the import service checks format automatically; the operator reviews the report only on failure. Uniform rewrite: Check the file format. Review the error report.

not_allowed.rationale: The copied imperative pattern assigns an automatic action to the reader and removes the failure condition. Surface consistency cannot justify either change.

facets.source_facet: Repeated procedure types are easier to recognize when equivalent steps reuse terminology and wording.
facets.rationale: Reuse reviewed IT terms and sentence patterns only after checking semantic and contextual equivalence.

facets.source_facet: Descriptive writing requires logical structure and coherence across the complete explanation.
facets.rationale: Keep description coherent instead of mechanically applying a repeated step template.

criteria: Review both procedural reuse and descriptive coherence against ASD-STE100 Issue 9 rule 9.4, physical PDF pages 122-123.
Compare actors, conditions, timing, quantities, scope, effects, and product context before accepting reused wording. Verify local term authority and any mappings to exact external labels.

Review original English authorship, examples, exceptions, applicability, separate ASD rights, attribution, and planning references. Automated structure checks do not establish semantic equivalence or approve a template.

attribution.name: Aerospace, Security and Defence Industries Association of Europe (ASD)

rights.scope: original IT-STE wording and examples only; ASD source rights remain separate
